- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to lower historical levels too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10 days) are systematically underestimated, indicating lag in capturing downward momentum.
- Forecasts exhibit high volatility in the middle of the 30d window, often peaking in the 15–20th day, which correlates with true outcomes showing a downward correction.
- Model fails to account for sharp downward corrections after high peaks — especially in the 20–30 day range.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 5–7 days, suggesting asymmetric bias.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when recent history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 65–70 range), suggesting failure to recognize trend continuation.
